name: XBAEU Ku720-2 mobile sensing radar (Raytheon)
description: Scaled Ku720-2 distributed mobile sensing radar. CRS records it as the radar on the single-Stryker M-LIDS Increment 2.1, in place of KuMRFS. RTX states 360 deg persistent detection, identification and tracking. NO range figure of any type is published: the ring is a REPRESENTATIVE planning value from the app role-default table, not an XBAEU performance figure.

classifyRangeM.source: RTX (Raytheon) news release, 'RTX's Raytheon demos KuRFS and Coyote performance against complex UAS threats'

rangeAccuracyM.note: Planning factor: 10 m for a Ku-band fire-control waveform; no fire-control radar in the library publishes a figure and the nearest sourced Ku-band panel (EchoShield) gives 0.75 to 6 m.

azimuthAccuracyDeg.note: Planning factor: about a tenth of a 1.5 to 2° Ku-band AESA beam, so 0.2°; no fire-control radar in the library publishes a figure and the nearest sourced Ku-band panel (EchoShield) gives <0.5°.

elevationAccuracyDeg.note: Planning factor: about a tenth of a 1.5 to 2° Ku-band AESA beam, so 0.2°; no fire-control radar in the library publishes a figure and the nearest sourced Ku-band panel (EchoShield) gives <0.5°.

falseAlarmRatePerScan.note: Planning factor: PLACARD_PFA 1e-6 (src/model/types.ts) times about 1e6 range-azimuth-Doppler cells per scan of a 360° surveillance volume gives about one false alarm per scan over the whole coverage; this 360° radar is recorded at 1. No vendor publishes a false-alarm rate.

dwellTimeS.note: Planning factor: RTX publishes no dwell or CPI. An electronically scanned radar sets its dwell in the beam schedule rather than by beamwidth over scan rate; the literature CPI of 20 ms for X/Ku-band drone-detection AESAs is used. Open literature on X/Ku-band drone-detection AESAs gives a CPI of about 20 ms at 5 kHz PRF (about 100 pulses; arXiv 2307.10326) and about 30 ms at 6 kHz (about 180 pulses; MDPI Drones 7(5):316), and notes that a 2.7 ms dwell barely resolves micro-Doppler.

pulsesPerDwell.note: Planning factor: RTX publishes no PRF or pulse count. 20 ms dwell at the literature 5 kHz PRF gives 100 pulses coherently integrated. Open literature on X/Ku-band drone-detection AESAs gives a CPI of about 20 ms at 5 kHz PRF (about 100 pulses; arXiv 2307.10326) and about 30 ms at 6 kHz (about 180 pulses; MDPI Drones 7(5):316), and notes that a 2.7 ms dwell barely resolves micro-Doppler.
